audit_after: the terminal, because the growth storage that rides with it moves no number on this name and the two are one rule's worth of evidence rather than two

levers.name: terminal built through the sanctioned module on a life DERIVED by identity from notes 9, 10 and 13, on the LAST EXPLICIT YEAR as the module requires
levers.why: the terminal carried 81% of enterprise value on rr = g/ROIC, which charges g x IC for ever and implies replacing the whole base every 1/g = 25.0 years — a fact about a 4% nominal terminal, not about a cable plant this base turns over in 35.76 years. THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS LEVER READ +1.97% AND WAS WRONG: it handed the module a NOPAT already grown by (1+g), which the module grows again, overstating the terminal by exactly 4.00%. Corrected, the sanctioned terminal is 23,961 against the retired 24,350 — BELOW it, not above
levers.evidence: blended life 3,053,446,083 of gross cost over 85,395,637 of charge = 35.7565 years, the three charges summing to exactly the D&A this model carries; validated on the one leg with a single disclosed life, software at 14.43 derived against a stated 15. Terminal 24,350 -> 23,961 (-1.60%)

levers.name: terminal growth stored as a REAL rate on the house Saudi path, nominal derived
levers.why: a typed nominal rate is unfalsifiable. Stored as +1.96% real on a 2.00% house terminal it recomputes to 4.00% to the basis point, so NOTHING MOVES and what a reader gains is sight of the claim: this business is assumed to grow about two per cent a year in real terms for ever
levers.evidence: the study's own prior review argued this was coupled to the terminal and could not ship, on the ground that ZEROING the real growth would leave a 4.2-point convergence gap. The rule requires a stated real growth to be written down, not zeroed; the gap is unchanged at 2.2 points

levers.name: the age the maintenance charge rests on MEASURED off the notes rather than assumed at half the useful life
levers.why: the construction escalates the book charge over the AGE of the base, and half the useful life is that age only under uniform vintages. This base is not: an old plant and a young accounting system blend to 21.95 years against 17.88. This name is one of only two in six where the accounts permit the measurement at all — the other four deduct residual values or were assembled by acquisition
levers.evidence: note 9 accumulated depreciation 1,775,547,325 over a charge of 76,616,111 = 23.17 years, note 10 amortisation 29,319,636 over 5,603,548 = 5.23, charge-weighted 21.95. Maintenance +8.4%; terminal 23,961 -> 23,669

note: Several levers serving ONE rule are one piece of evidence, not several. `rules` combines them; `levers` keeps the order they were applied in so the route can be walked.
